newsitem.title: UK: Computer problems add to woes on IPE natgas contract.
newsitem.headline: Computer problems add to woes on IPE natgas contract.

text.p: The IPE March natural gas contract closed lower on Monday, the second day of trading on the contract, as expected, but trade was so thin as to make comment on the price meaningless, brokers said.

In a disappointing day's trade, computer problems struck in the afternoon to hamper liquidity, following a morning in which two trades in November had been "bust" by the exchange because of an error in entering details.

Trade was only seen in three periods, March, July and August, and only 40 contracts were traded over the whole day. And given that the minimum lot size is for five contracts of 1,000 therms a day each, the total volume of trade was described as "only a handful."
March fell by 0.805 pence a therm and July by 0.45 pence while August was up by 0.140 pence, but few players were focusing closely on the price.

"The busted trades put people off, and computer problems this afternoon didn't help," said a broker. But he added that there was still a reasonable depth to bids and offers seen, even if the gap between the two sides was wide and very little trade was done.
"Tomorrow will hopefully be better," he added, agreeing that Monday had been a disappointment.

The IPE confirmed that it had bust two trades in the morning session after a screen user entered a bid of 90 pence a therm for November instead of nine pence. This triggered the acceptance of offers at 12.95 pence and 19.25 pence, both of which were subsequently set aside.
